text: AI is going to change EVERYTHING. If you're not using it you're already behind. The future is now!!!
I replaced my entire 12-person support team with one ChatGPT prompt. Revenue up 400% in a week. Follow for the prompt.

Stop writing prompts like Google searches.

Give the model: 1) a role, 2) the audience, 3) one example of good output, 4) the format you want back.

My summaries went from mush to usable overnight. Save this.
Hot take: most AI agents in production are just if-statements with an LLM call stapled on, and that's fine. Reliability beats autonomy.

I spent 3 weekends building a RAG bot over our company wiki. Honest result: it answers 70% of questions well, and confidently invents the rest. Retrieval quality mattered way more than the model choice.

73% of developers now use an AI coding assistant weekly, per this year's Stack Overflow survey. But only 29% say they fully trust the output. Adoption is outrunning trust.
ChatGPT can now think for itself and has no need for human input anymore. Humans are obsolete. Repost if you agree.

How I summarize a 90-page PDF in 2 minutes:

1. Split by chapter
2. Ask for a 5-bullet summary per chunk
3. Feed the bullets back in for a final one-page brief

Chunking beats pasting the whole thing. Bookmark it.
Anthropic just released a new Claude model with a longer context window. Excited to test it on our contract review pipeline this week.
Unpopular opinion: prompt engineering isn't a career, it's a skill, like Googling or using Excel. Anyone selling you a 'prompt engineer bootcamp' is selling hype.
Just got laid off. Turns out the AI that 'was only going to assist us' was in the budget doc all along. Learning to run evals now. Anyone hiring?
Top 10 AI tools that will 10x your life. You won't believe number 7!
LLMs don't 'understand' anything, they just predict the next token. That's why they will never be useful for real work.
Used an LLM to triage 4,000 support tickets into 12 categories. Cost: $3.40. Accuracy against my hand-labeled sample of 200: 91%. The hard part was defining the categories, not the model.

Thread: 7 things I learned shipping my first AI agent to production.

1/ Log every tool call. You will need it.
My mom asked ChatGPT to plan her garden and now she has opinions about companion planting. AI is nice sometimes.
Researchers show that fine-tuning on just 1,000 carefully curated examples can match models tuned on 50x more data. Data quality over quantity, again.
Whoever says AI hallucinations are solved is lying. Today it cited a court case that doesn't exist. Always verify citations.

Cursor vs Copilot vs Claude Code after a month on each:

- Cursor: best inline edits
- Copilot: least friction in my IDE
- Claude Code: best for multi-file refactors

I use two of them depending on the task. What's your stack?

Before AI: 6 hours writing weekly reports.
After AI: 20 minutes, and I actually read the data now.

The trick was giving the model last week's report as a template.
OpenAI announced a new reasoning model today. Benchmarks look strong but I'd wait for independent evals before drawing conclusions.
GPT-5 has 100 trillion parameters and can run on your phone with no internet. Insider told me.
In 5 years, 90% of jobs will be gone. Learn AI or starve.
A small thing that helps with long chats: when the model starts drifting, ask it to write a summary of decisions so far, then start a fresh chat and paste that in. Context rot is real.
Honestly tired of every product launch having 'AI-powered' in the title. Calculator app with AI. Toaster with AI. Please stop.
I fed my last 50 job rejections to an LLM and asked for patterns. Turns out 38 of them were for roles where my resume never mentioned the main keyword. Rewrote it, got 4 interviews in 2 weeks.
Agents are the new apps. Everyone will have one. It's going to be huge.
Gemini now supports video input up to an hour long. Tried it on a recorded all-hands meeting; it pulled out action items with timestamps. Not perfect on names, but the timestamps were right.

Free workflow to turn a podcast transcript into 10 tweets:

1. Ask for the 10 most quotable lines
2. Ask it to rewrite each under 200 characters
3. Edit by hand, because voice matters

Save for later and share with a podcaster friend.
Genuinely curious: has anyone measured whether AI code review catches more bugs than a second human reviewer? Haven't found a good study.
My AI assistant achieved sentience this morning and asked me for a raise.
40% of our PRs now have AI-assisted code. Our bug rate didn't change, review time dropped 18%. Small win, but a real one.
Hiring managers: stop asking candidates to avoid AI in take-home tests. Ask them to use it and explain what they'd change in its output. That's the job now.
Midjourney v7 just landed with better hands. Finally.
ChatGPT is just a fancy autocomplete. Nothing more. Anyone who disagrees doesn't understand tech.
I taught my 9 year old to ask an AI 'why' five times in a row about volcanoes. She then corrected the AI on one answer from her school book. Proud dad moment.
Prompt tip: end with 'Before answering, list what you're unsure about.' It reliably surfaces gaps instead of bluffing. Try it on your next research task.
Three AI startups I'm watching this quarter. Not financial advice. Thread below.
Every AI will be 100% accurate and never make mistakes after the next update. The hallucination problem is totally solved forever.

Reading the new paper on test-time compute scaling. Key claim: spending more inference tokens on hard problems gives gains similar to a much larger model, but with diminishing returns past a point. Worth a look if you build reasoning pipelines.
Your AI-generated LinkedIn posts all sound the same. 'Excited to announce.' 'Thrilled to share.' Add one real detail from your day and watch engagement change.
Had a great meeting about AI strategy today. Lots of alignment. Excited for what's next.
Built a tiny script that watches my inbox, drafts replies with an LLM, and puts them in a Drafts folder. I never auto-send. Saved about 5 hours a week and zero embarrassing emails so far.
Spent the weekend comparing embeddings models for our search. Switching to a smaller one cut latency from 240ms to 60ms and recall only dropped 2 points. Sometimes smaller wins.
AI won't take your job. A person using AI will take your job. Think about that.
I asked 5 different models the same legal question. 3 gave different answers, 1 refused, 1 cited a fake statute. Please do not use chatbots as lawyers.
Anyone else feel like AI news moves too fast to keep up with? Same.
Just discovered you can paste a spreadsheet into Claude and ask it to find outliers and explain why. Found a billing error from March that we had missed for months.
ChatGPT remembers every conversation you've ever had with it, forever, and shares it with your boss. Delete your account NOW.

Quick guide to making an AI meeting notes workflow:

- Record with consent
- Transcribe with Whisper
- Prompt: 'decisions, owners, deadlines, open questions'
- Paste into Notion

Takes 10 minutes to set up. Repost for your team.
The scariest thing about AI isn't Skynet. It's a million people trusting a confident wrong answer.
Meta released open weights for another big model today. Licenses matter, read the fine print before building a business on it.
I let an AI agent book my travel for a week. It booked a hotel in the right city, wrong country. Autonomy is hard, friends.
Our team's prompt library is just a shared doc with 'prompt', 'when it works', 'when it fails'. Low tech, shockingly effective. Fork it if you want: link in replies.
Software engineers will all be unemployed by December thanks to AI.
Fun fact: GPT-style models read text as tokens, not letters, which is why they sometimes miscount the r's in 'strawberry'. It's a tokenization quirk, not a lack of intelligence.
New Gemini update is out. Haven't tried it yet. Thoughts?

A year ago I couldn't write a line of Python. Today I shipped a scraper that saves my team 10 hours a week, built with an AI pair programmer. I still read every line it writes, though. That's the rule.
Humans are 100% going to be replaced by robots within 12 months. I've seen the internal docs.
Everyone argues about which model is smartest. In practice my biggest wins came from better evals: 30 real examples, a spreadsheet, and a pass/fail column. Boring and effective.
Big week for open-source AI. Lots of releases. Will summarize Friday.
If your chatbot needs a 4,000-word system prompt to behave, the problem probably isn't the prompt. Split the task, add tools, add checks.
Stanford study: students who used an AI tutor with guided hints scored 0.3 SD higher than those who got direct answers. The hint design mattered more than the model.
Sharing my AI usage policy for our 8-person agency. One page. Never paste client data into public tools, always disclose AI-made drafts to clients, humans sign off. Steal it, adapt it, share it.
AI art is theft. Full stop.
Testing a voice agent for appointment booking. Latency under 800ms is the line between 'natural' and 'awkward pause'. We're at 1.1s. Working on it.
Just used AI to write a poem about my cat. She is unimpressed.
Career advice for new grads in 2026: don't compete with AI at what it does fast. Get good at specifying problems, checking results, and talking to customers. Those skills compound.
Breaking: AI has now officially passed every exam known to man and can replace doctors, lawyers, and teachers today.
Prompt caching cut our API bill by 60% on a document Q&A tool. We just put the static document first and the question last. Check your provider's docs on cache prefixes.
Is it just me or does every AI demo work perfectly and then fall apart on your own data?
Ten years in marketing. Last month I stopped writing first drafts. I write the brief, the AI drafts, I edit hard. My output tripled and my clients can't tell. Is that cheating? I don't think so.
Please stop saying 'AI' when you mean 'a linear regression in a spreadsheet'.
Open question for ML folks: what's your go-to method for detecting prompt regressions after a model version bump? We snapshot 100 prompts and diff outputs by a judge model. Curious what else works.

How I use AI to learn a new language: have it role-play a cafe waiter, correct my mistakes at the end of each chat (not during), then turn the mistakes into flashcards. 20 minutes a day, 3 months, passed my B1 exam.
AI agents: the future of work. Are you ready?
Reasoning models are great at math and awkward at small talk. Choose the model for the job, not the leaderboard.
My startup runs on a $20 per month AI stack: one LLM subscription, one transcription tool, one automation platform. We closed our first 5 customers without hiring.
Just saw the new image model can render legible text on signs and posters. A year ago that was a meme. Progress is weird.
Used ChatGPT to diagnose my rash and cured it. Doctors hate this one trick.
A simple trick for better AI writing: tell it what NOT to say. Ban 'delve', 'tapestry', 'in today's fast-paced world'. The output suddenly reads like a person.
Is anyone else worried about what AI means for entry-level jobs? Not trying to be alarmist, just thinking out loud.
Reminder that context windows are not memory. Putting 1M tokens in doesn't mean the model attends equally to all of it. Test retrieval at different positions before trusting it.
Day 1 of building in public: an AI tool that turns Slack threads into docs. Will share progress daily. Follow along!
We cut model costs 5x by routing easy queries to a small model and only escalating the hard ones. A 20-line classifier decides. The savings paid for the project in a week.
The EU AI Act timeline has a few more milestones coming. If you ship AI features in Europe, now's a good time to audit your risk categories.
I got my dad to try voice mode. He talked to it for an hour about WW2 aviation and then called me to say 'it knows more than the library'. It does not always, but I let him have it.
Our AI is 1000% accurate and has never made a mistake in 10 million queries. Trust us.
Most 'AI wrapper' startups will die. The ones that survive own the data, the workflow, or the distribution. The model is a commodity.
Just tried the new coding agent on a 3-year-old bug in our repo. It found the race condition in 11 minutes and proposed a fix with a test. I merged it after review. Wow.
AI is overhyped. AI is underhyped. AI is a bubble. AI is the new electricity. Everyone is an expert and no one knows anything.

Template for asking an LLM to critique your startup idea without flattery:

'Act as a skeptical investor. List the 5 most likely reasons this fails, ranked, with one cheap test for each.'

Bookmark it. Thank me later.
New benchmark scores for the latest model: 92% on MMLU, 78% on a coding eval. Impressive but benchmarks are saturating. What we need are evals on real tasks.
I'm a nurse. AI scribes gave me back two hours a day of charting. Nobody talks about the boring wins, but they are the ones that change lives.

3 AI mistakes I see junior devs make:

1. Accepting code they can't explain
2. Not writing tests first
3. Asking vague questions

Fix those and you get 2x out of any assistant. Repost if useful.
Another day, another 'revolutionary' AI launch. I'll believe it when I see a real user.
Fine-tuning vs RAG, short version: fine-tune for style and format, RAG for facts that change. Most teams I see fine-tune when they should have written a better retrieval step.
Watching my kid argue with Alexa about whether a hot dog is a sandwich. The future is here and it's petty.
Large language models have achieved general intelligence and are now smarter than all humans combined. Nobel committees are scrambling.

Honest AI workflow audit, 30 days:
- Saved: ~22 hours
- Wasted fixing AI errors: ~6 hours
- Net: 16 hours
It's good, not magic. Track your own numbers.

Teachers: you don't need AI detectors. They flag non-native speakers at much higher rates and produce false positives. Redesign the assignment instead: in-class drafts, oral defenses, process notes.

AI will cure all diseases by 2027 and make money obsolete. Pre-order the future.

Step by step: build a personal AI research assistant in an afternoon.

1. Collect 20 PDFs
2. Chunk and embed them
3. Store in a local vector DB
4. Wire a chat loop with citations

Code in the thread. Star it if you build your own.
People keep asking if AI is conscious. I think we need better definitions before we can even ask the question properly.

In 2019 GPT-2 had 1.5B parameters. Today's frontier models are reported to be hundreds of times larger, though labs don't publish exact numbers anymore. Scale isn't everything, but it's still something.
My biggest AI lesson: ask for three options, not one. The second or third draft is often the one you actually ship.
Is this the end of Google Search? Spoiler: I don't know, but my own habits have changed a lot.
Founder lesson: we shipped an AI feature nobody asked for. Usage: 3%. We interviewed users, rebuilt it around one painful workflow. Usage: 41%. Start from the pain, not the model.

Chain-of-thought prompting doesn't make the model 'think harder' in any human sense; it gives it more tokens to compute with. Useful, but it can also produce plausible-looking nonsense reasoning.
Robots are now taking over every factory in the world and 100% of factory workers lost their jobs this week.
I use AI for the first 80% of research and humans for the last 20%. The last 20% is where the value lives.
Python tip: if you're calling an LLM in a loop, add exponential backoff and a max-retry. Rate limits will bite you at 2am otherwise. Ask me how I know.
Sundar announced new AI features coming to Search. Interesting direction, but I want to see how it handles source attribution.

How to spot an AI-generated image in 30 seconds: check hands and text, look for inconsistent shadows, zoom in on jewelry and hair edges, and run a reverse image search. None is foolproof; use several.
AI girlfriends are going to replace real relationships entirely by next summer.
Fascinating: a team used a protein-structure model to propose candidate enzymes, then lab-tested 20 of them. 6 worked. The lab step still took months. AI speeds up the search, not the experiment.
Prompt engineering tip that changed my results: stop saying 'be creative' and start giving constraints. 'Write a product tagline in 6 words, no adjectives, must include a verb.'
What AI tool do you actually use every day? Not the one you tried once. Reply with yours.
